title: Replicating the Refusal Direction Across Smaller Open Models

original_idea.body: Extract and ablate/add the difference-of-means refusal direction in three 1-2B open chat models, reproducing Arditi metrics, and cross-apply directions across models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: One-line refusal-ablation jailbreak on tiny locally-misusable models is directly safety-relevant; defensible chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TransformerLens difference-of-means extraction on 1-2B models; well-documented inherited methodology, beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped replication: extract/ablate/add refusal direction on 3 small models + cross-transfer.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Tiny open models defenders can't control, no internal access; replication/auditing externally valuable.

low_compute.reasoning: 1-2B models; CPU/free-tier or single small GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Direct replication of a well-known result on smaller models; the cross-transfer twist adds modest novelty.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Replicates a well-established single-direction-refusal result on smaller models; the cross-model transfer twist adds a little novelty.
